tools.name: list_cities
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which cities WonderKit covers or needs a valid city key. Lists cities that have a published city guide of real things to do, with their keys. Reads public guides only; it cannot plan, save, or look up a private trip.

tools.name: find_activities
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what to do in one city: weekend ideas, events, food, or kid-friendly, date-night, or group activities. Returns published picks from the WonderKit city guide and the page URL. Returns single activities, not multi-day plans, and cannot see anyone's own trips.

tools.name: list_itineraries
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to browse WonderKit's public multi-day itineraries and place guides, for all cities or one city and audience. tools.description: Use this when someone wants to start planning their own trip to a destination in WonderKit. tools.name: continue_in_wonderkit
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to save, share, or keep working on a plan from a public guide or itinerary. Returns the WonderKit web links for that city guide, itinerary, and the guest planner. This server cannot save or share anything itself.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_itinerary · Private data: list_cities · Public sink: continue_in_wonderkit.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_itinerary · Private data: list_cities · Public sink: continue_in_wonderkit

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
